title: Enterprise Deal Pricing Guardrails & Security Questionnaire Pricing Evaluation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Create a concise, operational set of pricing guardrails for enterprise deals that ties discount approval thresholds and pricebook updates to risk signals surfaced by Security Questionnaires (SQs) and deployment requirements. This ticket covers: (1) a recommended discount matrix by ARR/term/deployment type; (2) rules for when security posture (from SQ) should reduce allowable discounts or trigger additional fees (e.g., private on-prem, dedicated, SOC2+ requirements); (3) an approval/escalation workflow for sales to request exceptions; (4) a small experiment to test revised guardrails on incoming enterprise opportunities for 6 weeks; and (5) updates to the internal pricebook and a readme for Sales/RevOps/Legal.
acceptance_criteria: A decision-ready discount matrix document that maps ARR bands, term length, and deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private) to default discount caps and approval tiers.

A one-page SQ-to-pricing mapping that defines which SQ answers increase price risk score (Low/Medium/High) and the corresponding pricing actions (reduce max discount by X%, add security surcharge, or require legal/engineering review).
A documented approval escalation flow with explicit approvers by threshold (Sales Manager, RevOps, Head of GTM, CFO) and sample Slack/email templates for exception requests.

A short pilot plan (6 weeks) with instrumentation: fields in CRM to capture 'SQ risk score', 'requested discount', 'approved discount', and links to dashboards tracking win-rate, ACV, and margin impact.
Pricebook change PR and confirmation that Sales enablement materials (FAQ, 1-pager) are published to the internal drive.
Legal and Security have provided sign-off on the SQ-to-pricing mapping and escalation triggers (security_review_required = true).
notes_and_decisions: 2025-02-20: Kickoff with Sales, RevOps, Legal, Security. Agreed scope to keep first iteration prescriptive (guardrails) rather than prescriptive discounts for individual SEs.

2025-02-27: Provisional discount caps agreed: up to 20% for ARR < $250k, up to 15% for ARR $250k–$1M, up to 10% for ARR > $1M on standard hosted deployments. Private/on-prem and Dedicated default to 5% lower caps unless justified by committed term or volume.

2025-03-03: Security suggested three SQ risk buckets. Action: product to draft mapping with Security to translate technical answers (data residency, encryption at rest, pen test cadence, third-party auditors) into a risk score.
Trade-offs discussed: stricter guardrails reduce deal velocity but protect margins and operational burden for private deployments. Team prefers a pilot with ex-post review before broad enforcement.
We will avoid hard-coded dollar thresholds in the initial release to keep flexibility across geos; use ARR bands and percentage caps instead.

Reference docs created: Confluence draft (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRG/pages/Enterprise+Pricing+Guardrails), drive doc for Sales enablement (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-pricing-playbook), CRM instrumentation spec (https://docs.redwood.com/crm/pricing-instrumentation).
